title: Eating habits ruin Oliver's stomach and his playing declines
summary: Stories of Oliver's meals, including eating a duck with Louis, and his stomach trouble leading him to miss band dates.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Yeah. So he didn't drink or didn't do nothing like that. The thing he liked was plenty of food. We played a town out in West Virginia called... What was the name of that town? One of them coal mine towns. A little small town. We got in at a barbecue place; we called it the Barbecue, where we played. A lady fixed breakfast for us that morning, and she had hot biscuits and fried rabbit and fried chicken, home-fried potatoes, butter, we had a big bowl of pear preserves... He eat about a whole pan of biscuits, then gave the lady a dollar more to fix him something to take with him. Yeah!

Then, too, when the bands first started getting bad, he started having a bad stomach. His stomach started to get into trouble. It's all that stuff he'd eat. I remember back in Tennessee, he ate six pig feet. Six pig feet... Oh, he could eat that with a half a loaf of bread and...

I remember one time in Chicago (I guess this would have been in the paper; a lot of told it), he used to go in the dressing room with a loaf of bread and sugar. He'd eat that with sugar. He said one time he and Louis eat up a whole duck; in one meal, he and Louis eat the duck up, and didn't have nothin' left for his wife. He said (heh) both of them got ashamed. He said Louis could eat... Louis would eat along with him in them days. They used to eat, and see who could eat the most, and all that kind of thing. But Louis got off of it. Because Louis got kind of fat, too, once. But Louis got off of it. It's (?) that he did, too. You see, in his stomach... He used to eat like that, and he'd say, "Oh, my stomach's achin' so bad." All that food! He had too much in there, you know.

So then he started drifting. Drifting down, you know what I mean? He couldn't play nothin'... He couldn't play, and so a lot of times he wouldn't be on the band playing, and they'd say, "Where is King Oliver?" He'd be at home.
